subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: What durable Mattermost interaction-signing credential model should replace the current bot-token-derived HMAC secret?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes the security boundary plus setup and upgrade behavior for Mattermost button callbacks.

options.title: Provision A Durable Per-Account Secret
options.body: Persist or configure a per-account interaction secret through supported setup, SecretRef, docs, and tests so sender and verifier share it across restarts and processes.

options.title: Fail Closed Until Configured
options.body: Require operators to configure an interaction secret explicitly and make the missing-secret failure mode clear in runtime messages, docs, and tests.

options.title: Pause For Security Design
options.body: Keep the issue and linked PR open while a maintainer-owned security design decides where this credential should live.

recommendation.title: Provision A Durable Per-Account Secret
recommendation.body: Persist or configure a per-account interaction secret through supported setup, SecretRef, docs, and tests so sender and verifier share it across restarts and processes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent hardening work on Mattermost callback binding makes this the strongest routing signal for the security-boundary decision.
